blocks.text: Home Restorations: Preserve Character. Add Longevity. Paint the Right Way.

Craftsman homes are among the most cherished architectural styles in the Pacific Northwest. With their overhanging eaves, tapered columns, wood siding, and historic charm, these homes speak to another era—one of thoughtful design and enduring quality.
But if you own a Craftsman or older home in Tacoma, Bonney Lake, or surrounding Puget Sound neighborhoods, maintaining that character often comes down to how you prep and paint.

At Black Pearl Painters, we specialize in older home restoration painting, with a strong emphasis on proper prep, surface repair, and historic color matching. Whether your home dates to the early 1900s or just reflects a classic Craftsman style, this guide will help you understand the essential steps for a lasting, beautiful finish.
Why Painting Older Homes Requires a Different Approach

Unlike modern construction, older homes come with unique challenges: aged wood, lead-based paint, multiple layers of coatings, and intricate architectural details. Painting over these without the right prep not only risks peeling and failure, but it can also damage the home’s historic value.
Craftsman homes often include:

items: Wood lap siding or cedar shingles

blocks.text: Each of these elements needs careful attention before paint is applied. Quick, modern methods simply don’t cut it.
Step 1: Inspection and Surface Assessment
Every successful older home restorations and painting project starts with a full inspection of the exterior. At Black Pearl Painters, we examine:

items: Wood condition – checking for rot, warping, or insect damage
Previous coatings – identifying flaking, chipping, or incompatible layers
Moisture damage – especially in rooflines, eaves, and near ground contact
Lead paint risks – for homes built before 1978, lead-safe practices are required

blocks.text: Failing to inspect these issues can cause even premium paints to fail prematurely.
Step 2: Professional Paint Prep for Historic Exteriors

Proper paint prep for Craftsman homes is labor-intensive but essential for long-term results. Unlike newer builds that may only need a light wash and scuff, older home restorations require several key steps:
Power Washing (Low-Pressure for Delicate Areas)
We start by cleaning the surface to remove mildew, dirt, and loose material. On delicate trim or weathered siding, we may use low-pressure washing or even hand washing to avoid water intrusion.
Paint Removal & Scraping

Where peeling is severe or multiple layers exist, hand scraping and sanding are used to feather edges and smooth the surface. In cases of lead-based paint, EPA-certified containment and disposal procedures are followed.
Surface Repairs & Carpentry
Rotten trim, cracked siding, or missing shingles? We offer on-site carpentry repair to replace damaged wood with matching profiles. This prevents future decay and restores original details.
Caulking & Sealing
Gaps around windows, doors, and trim are filled with high-quality exterior caulk, creating a weathertight seal that enhances both appearance and performance.

blocks.text: Step 3: Primer Selection for Aged Wood
Older wood can be dry, porous, and full of tanning, especially if it’s redwood or cedar. That’s why primer selection is critical.

items: Oil-based primers often work best for bare wood or areas previously painted with oil
Stain-blocking primers prevent bleed-through from water stains, tannins, or rust
Bonding primers ensure proper adhesion on slick or chalky surfaces

blocks.text: We always tailor the primer to the surface, especially important when dealing with multiple surfaces like lap siding, vertical board, soffits, and fascia.
Step 4: Color Matching for Craftsman Charm

One of the most important, and often stressful, parts of painting an older home is choosing the right color palette. Craftsman homes are known for their earth-toned hues, inspired by nature and the Arts & Crafts movement.
Popular Craftsman Color Palettes:

items: Forest green with cream and burgundy trim
Olive or sage with rust-red and tan accents
Charcoal with pale gray and rich wood-tone highlights

blocks.text: At Black Pearl Painters, we help you either match the original paint scheme (through color matching tools or historic records) or create an updated palette that respects the home’s heritage.
We use Sherwin-Williams historic color collections and digital mockups to preview your choices before painting begins.
Step 5: Choosing the Right Paint
For older homes in the damp Puget Sound climate, durability matters just as much as aesthetics.
We recommend Sherwin-Williams Duration® or Emerald® exterior paints, which offer:

items: Exceptional adhesion on older, textured surfaces
Flexible film that moves with expanding and contracting wood

blocks.text: These high-performance paints ensure your home stays protected for years to come, while showcasing its original beauty.
Step 6: The Craft of Application
Vintage homes deserve a craftsman’s touch; not a rushed spray job. Depending on the surface, we use:

items: Back-brushing techniques to work paint into textured or porous wood
Hand-painting on trim and details for clean, crisp edges
Controlled spray and roll combos where appropriate for efficiency without sacrificing coverage

blocks.text: The result is a cohesive, professionally restored exterior that maintains the home’s identity while protecting it for decades.
